## Why asking the right questions matters  
Choosing an SEO partner without a clear questionnaire leads to mismatched expectations and wasted budget. A structured set of questions lets you compare providers on process, cost, and compliance before any contract is signed.

Govindani Infotech Pvt. Ltd. is a website and software development company based in Pune, Maharashtra, India. The same disciplined approach that we use for software projects applies to evaluating SEO agencies: define outcomes, verify capabilities, and lock in transparent terms.

### The cost of guesswork in SEO  
When you sign an SEO contract based on marketing fluff, the most common pitfalls are vague deliverables, hidden fees, and unrealistic timelines. Indian NGOs and small businesses often operate on tight cash flow, so a mis‑aligned engagement can jeopardise core operations.

### How a questionnaire protects your ROI  
A well‑crafted questionnaire forces the agency to disclose methodology, reporting cadence, and any third‑party tools they rely on. That transparency lets you calculate a realistic return on investment in rupees, factoring in GST and any ancillary expenses.

## Understanding the provider’s process and methodology  
A reputable SEO firm follows a documented, repeatable process that starts with discovery and ends with measurable outcomes. Look for agencies that can walk you through each phase in plain language.

### Discovery and audit  
The first step should be a technical SEO audit of your site, a competitor gap analysis, and a keyword research brief. An audit report typically includes crawl errors, page‑speed scores, and a list of high‑potential keywords relevant to Indian search behaviour.

### Strategy formulation  
After the audit, the agency should present a strategic plan that outlines on‑page optimisation, content creation, link‑building tactics, and local SEO actions (e.g., Google My Business optimisation for Maharashtra). Ask how they prioritise tasks and what timeline they propose for each milestone.

### Execution and iteration  
Execution involves content creation, technical fixes, and outreach. The provider should explain how they test changes (e.g., A/B testing meta titles) and how they adjust tactics based on performance data. Iteration is essential because Google’s algorithm updates affect rankings regularly.

### Measurement and reporting  
Ask for the specific KPIs they track—organic traffic, keyword rankings, conversion rate, and revenue‑per‑click are common. The agency should provide monthly reports in a format you can read without a specialist, ideally with visual dashboards that show trends over the past 30, 60, and 90 days.

## Evaluating experience and track‑record in the Indian market  
SEO success is highly contextual; a strategy that works for a US e‑commerce brand may not translate to a Pune‑based clinic. Verify the agency’s local expertise before committing.

### Portfolio of Indian clients  
Request case studies that include at least one client from a similar sector—NGO, D2C brand, school, clinic, or agency. Look for evidence of ranking improvements for Hindi or Marathi queries, as well as traffic growth from Indian IP addresses.

### Duration of operations and staff qualifications  
An agency that has been operating for three to five years in India is more likely to understand regional search trends, GST implications, and local content regulations. Inquire about the qualifications of the team members who will handle your account, such as certifications from Google Analytics, Google Ads, or industry‑recognised SEO courses.

### References and client feedback  
While we cannot share specific client names, a trustworthy provider will offer at least two references who can speak to delivery, communication, and post‑project support. A pattern of consistent positive feedback is a stronger indicator than a single glowing testimonial.

## Clarifying deliverables, reporting, and communication  
Clear deliverables prevent scope creep and ensure you receive the services you pay for. Documenting communication channels also reduces misunderstand‑ings.

### Scope of work (SOW) details  
Ask the agency to list every item they will deliver: number of SEO‑optimised pages per month, blog posts, backlink targets, and local citation submissions. The SOW should also state what is **not** included, such as paid advertising or website redesign, unless explicitly added.

### Reporting cadence and format  
Monthly reports are standard, but some agencies also provide a quarterly performance review. Confirm whether the reports will be delivered via email, a client portal, or a shared Google Sheet. Ask if they offer real‑time dashboards that you can access at any time.

### Points of contact and response time  
Identify a single account manager who will be your primary liaison. Ask about their typical response window for emails or Slack messages—most agencies aim for 24‑hour replies on business days.

### Change‑request procedure  
SEO projects evolve. The provider should have a documented process for handling change requests, including how additional work is priced and approved. This prevents surprise invoices later in the engagement.

## Pricing structure, contracts, and hidden costs  
Understanding the financial model helps you compare offers without getting blindsided by hidden fees or unfavourable contract terms.

### Common pricing models in India  
| Pricing Model | Typical Range (₹ per month) | What’s Included | Pros | Cons |
|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------|------|------|
| Fixed‑price retainer | 30,000 – 80,000 | Ongoing optimisation, reporting, limited content | Predictable cash flow, easy budgeting | May limit flexibility for large projects |
| Performance‑based | 20,000 + a % of revenue lift | Core SEO tasks, bonuses for ranking gains | Aligns incentives, lower upfront cost | Revenue attribution can be disputed |
| Project‑based | 50,000 – 150,000 (one‑time) | Site audit, technical fixes, initial content plan | Clear start‑end, good for quick wins | No ongoing optimisation, may need follow‑up |
| Hourly consulting | 1,500 – 3,500 per hour | Advisory, audit review, strategy tweaks | Pay only for time used | Hard to predict total cost |

These ranges depend on agency size, client industry, and the depth of services required. All Indian vendors must add 18 % GST to the quoted amount, which should be shown as a separate line item in the invoice.

### Contract length and renewal clauses  
Typical contracts run for six to twelve months, with an option to renew. Short‑term contracts may be cheaper but can limit the time needed for SEO to show results. Verify whether the provider charges an early‑termination fee and how notice periods are handled.

### Hidden costs to watch for  
- **Tool licences:** Some agencies charge extra for SEO tools like Ahrefs or SEMrush.  
- **Content creation:** Blog posts or copywriting may be billed per word or per article.  
- **Link‑building fees:** High‑quality backlinks often involve outreach costs.  
- **Additional audits:** Quarterly technical audits may be offered as an add‑on.

Ask for a full cost breakdown before signing, and confirm that all taxes, including GST, are included in the final figure.

## Compliance, security, and data privacy considerations  
Indian regulations such as the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures) Rules, 2011 and the Personal Data Protection Bill (when enacted) affect how SEO agencies handle your data.

### Data ownership and access  
The agency should state that all data—Google Analytics, Search Console, and keyword reports—remain your property. Verify that you will receive raw data exports upon request and that the provider does not lock you into a proprietary dashboard.

### Security of credentials  
Ask how the agency stores login credentials for your website, Google accounts, and hosting. Best practice is to use a password manager (e.g., LastPass) and to grant limited, time‑bound access rather than sharing permanent passwords.

### Compliance with Indian advertising standards  
If the agency runs any paid search or local citation campaigns, they must comply with the Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) guidelines. This is especially relevant for NGOs and educational institutions that must avoid misleading claims.

### GDPR vs. Indian privacy law  
Even though GDPR is a European regulation, many Indian agencies serve international clients and may follow its standards. Clarify whether the provider adheres to GDPR‑level safeguards, which can be an extra layer of protection for donor or patient data.

## How to assess ongoing support and performance guarantees  
SEO is a long‑term investment, and you need assurance that the agency will stay accountable after the initial milestones are met.

### Service level agreements (SLAs) for uptime and reporting  
An SLA may specify that monthly reports are delivered within five business days of month‑end, and that any critical website issue identified during optimisation is addressed within 48 hours. While SLAs are not mandatory, they provide measurable expectations.

### Performance guarantees and realistic timelines  
Beware of promises such as “first‑page ranking in 30 days.” A credible agency will instead set realistic milestones, like “target 10 % organic traffic growth over six months.” Ask how they calculate these targets and what factors could affect them (e.g., algorithm updates, seasonal demand).

### Post‑contract transition plan  
When the engagement ends, you should receive a hand‑over document that includes all credentials, a summary of work performed, and recommendations for next steps. This ensures continuity if you decide to bring SEO in‑house or switch providers.

### Ongoing education and knowledge transfer  
Some agencies offer quarterly webinars or training sessions for your internal team. This can be valuable for NGOs or schools that want to maintain a basic level of SEO competence after the contract expires.

## Comparison of key questions to ask an SEO provider  
The table below summarises the most important question categories, why they matter, and typical red‑flags to watch for. Use it as a checklist when you interview potential partners.

| Question Category | Sample Question | Why It Matters | Red‑Flag Indicator |
|-------------------|----------------|----------------|--------------------|
| Process & Methodology | “Can you walk me through your SEO workflow from audit to reporting?” | Reveals transparency and systematic approach | Vague answer, reliance on “proprietary magic” |
| Local Experience | “Do you have case studies for Indian NGOs or D2C brands?” | Confirms relevance to Indian search patterns | No local examples, only overseas clients |
| Deliverables | “What specific tasks will you complete each month?” | Prevents scope creep and hidden work | Open‑ended list, “as needed” language |
| Reporting | “What KPIs will you track and how will they be presented?” | Aligns expectations on measurable outcomes | Only “traffic” without conversion or revenue metrics |
| Pricing & GST | “What is the total monthly cost inclusive of GST and any add‑ons?” | Avoids surprise invoices | Separate line items for “tools” without disclosure |
| Contracts | “What is the minimum contract term and termination policy?” | Protects against lock‑in without exit | Early‑termination fee >30 % of remaining value |
| Data Security | “How do you store and share access credentials?” | Safeguards against breaches | “We keep everything on a shared spreadsheet” |
| Support & SLA | “What is your response time for critical issues?” | Ensures timely fixes for ranking‑critical problems | No defined SLA, “we’ll get back to you soon” |

## Frequently Asked Questions  

### What should I look for in an SEO audit for an Indian website?  
A solid audit checks crawlability, page‑speed (especially on mobile networks), structured data, and local signals like Google My Business. It should also highlight duplicate content and any penalties from Google’s Manual Actions.

### How long does it typically take to see organic traffic improvements in India?  
Organic growth usually becomes noticeable after three to six months of consistent optimisation, depending on competition, keyword difficulty, and the baseline health of the site. Seasonal industries may see quicker lifts during peak demand periods.

### Is it safe to share my Google Search Console access with an SEO agency?  
Yes, provided the agency uses a least‑privilege approach—granting “restricted” access rather than full owner rights. Ensure they use a password manager and that you can revoke access at any time.

### Do Indian SEO agencies need to charge GST on their services?  
All registered service providers in India must add 18 % Goods and Services Tax (GST) to their invoices. The GST amount should appear as a separate line item on the bill.

### Can I combine SEO with paid search for better results?  
Integrating SEO with Google Ads can accelerate data collection for keyword performance and improve overall visibility. However, the budgets for each channel should be planned separately, and the agency should clarify which activities fall under organic versus paid services.

### How often should I expect keyword ranking reports?  
Monthly reporting is standard, but some clients request bi‑weekly snapshots for high‑priority keywords. The key is to have a consistent cadence that matches your decision‑making cycle.

## Where to Start  
Begin by drafting a short questionnaire based on the comparison table above, then reach out to three shortlisted agencies for their written responses. Review each answer for clarity, specificity, and alignment with your budget and compliance needs. Once you have the information, schedule a brief call to clarify any gaps before requesting a formal proposal.
